spring-rest-sakila

The Spring REST Sakila project is a sample REST API service providing access to the MySQL Sakila database, a learning database that models a DVD rental store company. The service enables CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations and complex queries on data including films, actors, customers, rentals, payments, staff, stores, and location information. It demonstrates enterprise patterns and best practices for building a production-ready REST API with Spring Boot, including authentication, authorization, caching, and comprehensive API documentation.

🕐 Generated September 11, 2026 at 04:07 AM UTC
Technology Stack: Spring Boot Web Spring Data JPA Spring HATEOAS Spring REST Docs Spring Security Spring Actuator Spring Validation Lombok MapStruct Querydsl Blaze-Persistence MySQL Connector JJWT (JWT tokens) Redis Prometheus Asciidoctor (REST documentation)
The application follows a layered architecture organized around multiple domain modules (catalog, customer, location, payment, rental, staff, store, and authentication). Each domain contains controller, service, repository, mapper, entity, and DTO layers. The repository layer implements the custom repository pattern with both Spring Data JPA and Querydsl/Blaze-Persistence for complex queries. Services provide business logic and transactional boundaries. Controllers expose REST endpoints with HATEOAS support. Mappers handle bidirectional conversions between entities and DTOs. Cross-cutting concerns are managed through configuration classes for security, persistence, logging, and caching. The application uses Spring Security with JWT-based authentication and Spring Data REST conventions for API consistency.
Domain Modules: Catalog (Actor, Film, Category management) Customer (Customer information and queries) Location (Address, City, Country, Language management) Payment (Payment records and sales aggregations) Rental (Rental transactions and overdue tracking) Staff (Staff member management and details) Store (Store management, sales reports, and inventory) Authentication (User authentication, JWT tokens, and authorization)

package com.example.app.services.customer.controller
1 commit · last modified 2023-06-28
REST controller for managing customer resources, providing endpoints to retrieve, create, update, and delete customers, as well as access related payment and rental information. All operations require ROLE_MANAGE authorization.
GET /customers POST /customers GET /customers/{customerId} PUT /customers/{customerId} DELETE /customers/{customerId} GET /customers/{customerId}/details GET /customers/{customerId}/payments GET /customers/{customerId}/rentals

ResponseEntity getCustomerList(Pageable pageable) Retrieves a paginated list of all customers, supporting pagination through the Pageable parameter.

MethodDescription
CustomerDto mapToDto(CustomerEntity entity) Converts a CustomerEntity to a CustomerDto, ignoring the mapped relationship fields (storeByStoreId, addressByAddressId, authorityByAuthorityId).
CustomerEntity mapToEntity(CustomerDto dto) Converts a CustomerDto to a CustomerEntity, mapping firstName and lastName to nested fullName fields, setting lastUpdate to the current LocalDateTime, and ignoring auto-generated and relationship fields.
MapStruct mapper with Spring component model integration Uses expression-based mapping to set lastUpdate to LocalDateTime.now() at conversion time Nested field mapping: firstName/lastName from DTO map to fullName.firstName/lastName in entity Relationship fields (storeByStoreId, addressByAddressId, authorityByAuthorityId) are consistently ignored in both directions to prevent bidirectional cycles
